title: Inverse Functions
seo_title: Grade 12 Inverse Functions Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Definition of a function; general concept of the inverse of a function and how the domain of the function may need to be restricted (in order to obtain a one-to-one function) to ensure that the inverse is a function; determine and sketch graphs of the inverses of y = ax + q, y = ax² and y = bˣ (b > 0, b ≠ 1).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 inverse functions worksheets: inverses of straight lines, parabolas and exponential functions, and points on inverses. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Swap x and y, then make y the subject.
key_sub: (a; b) on f gives (b; a) on f⁻¹.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To find an inverse, swap x and y, then make y the subject.
  • The graph of f−1 is the reflection of f in the line y = x: (a; b) becomes (b; a).
  • y = ax² is not one-to-one, so restrict the domain (for example x ≥ 0) before taking the inverse.
  • The inverse of y = bˣ is y = logb x.

Examples

Example

f(x) = 3x − 6

x = 3y − 6

Answer: f⁻¹(x) = (x + 6)/3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not swappingSwap x and y first.
The domainRestrict y = ax² to x ≥ 0 or x ≤ 0.
logxIt is logb x.

items.q: A tutor charges R15 per hour plus a R20 booking fee, so C(h) = 15h + 20. Thabo paid R65. Use the inverse to find how many hours he booked.
items.e: The inverse is h = (C − 20) ÷ 15. (65 − 20) ÷ 15 = 3 hours.
An inverse swaps inputs and outputs: f(5) = −15 means f−1(−15) = 5.

items.q: The graph of an inverse function is the reflection of the original graph over which line?
items.e: Swapping x and y reflects every point over the line y = x. y = x.
An inverse swaps inputs and outputs: f(0) = −1 means f−1(−1) = 0.

c: No, because they have different gradients
items.e: f(g(x)) = 2 · x − 32 + 3 = (x − 3) + 3 = x. Yes, because f(g(x)) = x.

items.q: Why does f(x) = x² not have an inverse function on all real numbers?
c: Its graph is not a straight line
Two inputs give the same output, such as f(2) = f(−2)
items.e: A horizontal line meets the parabola twice, so it fails the horizontal line test. Two inputs give the same output, such as f(2) = f(−2).

items.q: Which function has an inverse that is also a function?
items.e: x³ passes the horizontal line test: each output comes from exactly one input. f(x) = x³.
